In [[geometry]], the '''Schiffler point''' of a [[triangle]] is a [[triangle center]], a point defined from the triangle that is [[equivariant]] under [[Euclidean transformation]]s of the triangle. This point was first defined and investigated by [[Kurt Schiffler|Schiffler]] et al. (1985).

==Definition==
A triangle {{math|△''ABC''}} with the [[incenter]] {{mvar|I}} has its Schiffler point at the point of concurrence of the [[Euler line]]s of the four triangles {{math|△''BCI'', △''CAI'', △''ABI'', △''ABC''}}. '''Schiffler's theorem''' states that these four lines all meet at a single point.<ref name="Emelyanov"/>

==Coordinates==
[[Trilinear coordinates]] for the Schiffler point are
:<math>\frac{1}{\cos B + \cos C} : \frac{1}{\cos C + \cos A} : \frac{1}{\cos A + \cos B}</math> <ref name="Emelyanov"/>
or, equivalently,
:<math>\frac{b+c-a}{b+c} : \frac{c+a-b}{c+a} : \frac{a+b-c}{a+b}</math>
where {{mvar|a, b, c}} denote the side lengths of triangle {{math|△''ABC''}}.
